gap: No result ChatGPT got states how bright these projectors are in the battery mode that gives their rated runtime. ProjectorCentral measured the XGIMI MoGo 4 at 151 ISO lumens in ECO, the mode behind its roughly 2.5-hour runtime, against 400 lumens in Performance. It measured the Nebula Mars 3 Air at 145 ANSI lumens in Eco, where it ran 3 h 10 min. The Nebula Mars 3 measured 298 lumens in Eco with Standard picture mode, the mode Anker rates for its 5-hour runtime.
standout_why: Both cited RTINGS pages (best/under-1000 and best/portable), the RTINGS MoGo 4 Laser review and the RTINGS MoGo 4 vs MoGo 4 Laser compare page all came back as navigation only when I opened them on 2026-11-14. None of their picks or figures loaded, so I could not check whether RTINGS gives battery-mode brightness. A search snippet suggested RTINGS' measured lumens and battery figures sit behind its paywall, but I did not confirm that on the page. ChatGPT's own answer puts 450/400/1,000 lumens next to 2.5 h or 5 h as if you get both at once, and says the figures are maker ratings. I did not open the uncited results (What Hi-Fi, Esquire, Wirecutter mirror and others). From their titles they are roundups; What Hi-Fi's reviews describe brightness in words rather than lumen figures, but I did not check those pages. The Hook Up's 2026 roundup (not in ChatGPT's results) covers the Mars 3 but not the MoGo 4, Mars 3 Air or GV50.
decides: This confirms the Mars 3 as the outdoor and camping pick, because on battery it keeps about double the light of the others. It measured 298 lm in Eco (Anker's 5-hour mode) and 785 lm in Standard picture at full power, while the Mars 3 Air (145 lm, Eco) and MoGo 4 (151 lm, ECO) are bedroom or dark-room projectors when running a full movie on battery. Between those two, the Mars 3 Air measured the longer Eco runtime (3 h 10 min against about 2.5 h). The MoGo 4 measured lower input lag in Game mode (22.1 ms against 44.1 ms). For the MoGo 4 Laser, the only measurement found is Expert Reviews' 1 h 53 min in Standard mode, so the $270 extra over the MoGo 4 does not buy longer runtime, and The Hook Up found its usable brightness essentially the same as the MoGo 4's.
